key_insight: A non-resonant acoustic streaming "wind" can unpin trapped oil droplets in capillary tubes when combined with static pressure gradients, with a derived optimal absorption condition that minimizes required drive power.
engineering_relevance: The model offers a design rule for low-power acoustic mobilization in porous media and downhole tools, helping optimize frequency and amplitude for droplet release in narrow channels.
method: Expanded the hydrodynamic equations to second order to capture acoustic-streaming force density.
Derived the critical acoustic amplitude needed to overcome capillary pinning.
Included wall-layer and bulk thermo-viscous dissipation to obtain an optimal absorption condition (α = 1/2x0).
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical validation of the optimal condition and cross-correlation against legacy industrial frequency baselines.
watch_item: The formulation is analytical and idealized, so real formations may deviate due to heterogeneous pore geometry, fluid properties, and dissipation losses.
paper_title: Unpinning of trapped oil droplets via non-resonant acoustic streaming in capillary tubes
